thread:
Maya (Support): Hey team, ACME is hitting intermittent 502s from our hosted inference endpoint since yesterday's cert rotation. They see TLS handshake timeouts and gateway errors in their logs. reported spike ~08:30 UTC.
Nick (Oncall): Ack. Do we have a customer request ID or example request/response?
Maya (Support): Elaine from ACME pasted a curl trace and our gateway trace ID: req-ACME-7791. Ela: 'curl --resolve' shows handshake timeouts from a handful of locations, but other regions are fine.
ACME Integrator: Confirming — around 08:28 UTC we started seeing 502/504s, clients retrying. Some requests get through. No auth failures, it's lower-level TLS/connectivity.
Sam (Infra): I'm pulling edge traces. There's a cluster in eu-west returning 502s with TLS handshake timeout code. Seeing SNI mismatch on a subset of connections.
Maya (Support): ACME also tried sdk v2.1 with ephemeral keys — same symptom, so not client token.
Nick (Oncall): Can ACME run an openssl s_client from affected host and paste output? Need to check server cert chain and SNI.
ACME Integrator: Pasted: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -servername api.redwood.example -timeout 5
CONNECTED(00000003)
139491... error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure
---
no peer certs
---
```
Nick (Oncall): That error usually means the other side closed before sending certs — could be mismatch in SNI or backend serving wrong cert. Sam, any certs recently rotated?
Sam (Infra): Yes, we rolled certs for gateway on 2339500000 UTC (canary -> global roll). Logs show that some edge nodes pulled new cert, others still serving old cert during propagation window.
Maya (Support): ACME attached a dig +short and a full trace. Their resolver sometimes returns an A record for an old load-balancer IP (10.23.45.67) which still had old certs, while the new LB IP (10.98.76.54) has the new cert.
resolver-bot: Automated note: DNS change for api.redwood.example performed at 2339499800, TTL=300. Zone change propagated to 70% of resolvers within first minute.
Nick (Oncall): Hmm — looks like a TTL/propagation overlap: some clients hit old LB with old cert chain; our gateway expects clients to use new cert. If the old LB is still up but serving a different cert (or not configured for SNI), handshake fails => 502s.
Elaine (Customer): Is there anything we can do from our side to mitigate right now? Our customers are panicking.
Maya (Support): Immediate mitigation: flush local DNS cache on affected hosts and restart clients; set OS resolver to use 1.1.1.1 temporarily to pick up updated A. Also disabling HTTP keepalive for retries short-term helped some clients.
ACME Integrator: We flushed cache, switched to 1.1.1.1, some clients recovered but mobile users still see issues in some carriers.
Sam (Infra): We're going to mark the old LB as deprecated and drain traffic out of it, then ensure it serves the same cert (or redirects) for a brief overlap next rotation. Rolling a compatibility patch now to serve both chains during transition.
Nick (Oncall): Also adding a monitoring check that verifies SNI/cert chain across all LB IPs and from multiple public DNS resolvers before and during cutover.
Maya (Support): Repro steps I documented for ACME and internal SRE: 
1) run `dig +trace api.redwood.example` from affected host
2) check returned A IPs, then `openssl s_client -connect <IP>:443 -servername api.redwood.example`
3) if handshake fails with no peer certs, try `curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.example:443:<IP>' https://api.redwood.example/health`
Include gateway trace id header `X-Request-ID: req-ACME-7791`.
ACME Integrator: We ran those; attached dig trace shows split-horizon/resolver cache returning both IPs.
Sam (Infra): For root cause timeline: cert rollout + DNS update to point to new LB happened within the same maintenance window. Some resolvers cached the old IP. Because old LB removed the old cert too quickly, some client TLS handshakes to that IP fail -> surfaced as gateway 502/504 upstream timeouts.
resolver-bot: Note: TTL=300 but some ISP resolvers ignore TTL and cache longer (observed up to 1800s).
Nick (Oncall): Action items:
- Infra: ensure LB back-compat cert serving during migrations (Sam)
- Infra: add pre-cutover multi-resolver cert check (Sam)
- Support: send ACME short mitigation steps and ETA (Maya)
- Customer: continue to report any specific CIDRs/carriers still failing (Elaine)
Maya (Support): Sent ACME mitigation steps and ETA ~20m.
Sam (Infra): Pushed hotfix to LB: old IP now serves both cert chains for 15m and then will gracefully drain. Rolling change should remove most 502s.
ACME Integrator: We're seeing error rate fall from 8% -> 0.7% in last 12m. Good improvement.
Nick (Oncall): Postmortem notes: we need a runbook for cert+DNS co-ordinated rollouts: ensure old IPs either remain configured with previous certs for a grace window, or we stage DNS with lower-risk phasing. Adding automated checks to deploy pipeline.
Maya (Support): Closing on support side, I created ticket S-233950-1 with logs. Will follow up with ACME once infra confirms full drain. :thumbsup:
Sam (Infra): Confirmed drain complete at 2339501600, monitoring stable. Will file infra follow-up for improved rollout tooling.
Elaine (Customer): Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick response!
Maya (Support): Filing a short KB entry for Support on 'cert rotation + DNS propagation' troubleshooting steps.
